_doc: Configuration for ollama-offload. `hosts.<name>` maps a logical name to an inference endpoint; `default_host` picks the active one. Environment overrides win over this file: OLLAMA_OFFLOAD_HOST selects which host entry to use, and OLLAMA_OFFLOAD_URL / _MODEL / _TIMEOUT_S / _TEMPERATURE / _CONTEXT_TOKENS / _THINK / _KEEP_ALIVE override individual fields. The OLLAMA_OFFLOAD_ prefix is deliberate: Ollama's own OLLAMA_HOST, OLLAMA_MODELS and OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE variables configure the Ollama server and CLI, and a library that read those would change behaviour for anyone who has them set for a different purpose. Input-size caps are DERIVED at runtime from the model's real context window, learned via /api/show, never hardcoded here -- per-consumer values below are RATIOS of that discovered window. Override a consumer with an absolute byte cap using its `max_input_bytes_override` key.

primary.notes: Fallback context is used only when /api/show does not report a window for the model.

secondary.notes: Example of a second host. Add it to failover_hosts, or set strategy to round-robin, to put it in the rotation.

_doc_think: Ollama's top-level /api/chat `think` field. Reasoning models default to thinking ON, which for a structured-JSON extraction contract adds latency without improving the result and can stall a call for the full timeout. Measured against a reasoning model: think=false returned in 1.5s where omitting the field hung past 180s. Per-call `think=` overrides this; so does OLLAMA_OFFLOAD_THINK.
_doc_keep_alive: "auto" (the default when this key is absent): conform to the loaded model. Every call re-arms the host's residency timer for the model it names, and an omitted field is not neutral. So send int -1 only when /api/ps shows the model already pinned Forever (expires_at year > 2100), and send no field otherwise; a client that sends -1 by default turns any short-lived load into a permanent pin on a shared GPU. An explicit value (int seconds, -1, or a duration string like "30m") is sent as given; null sends no field.
_doc_consumers: Each key below is a CONSUMER: a named caller with its own share of the context window. Pass its name as consumer= / -Consumer and the client sizes input against that ratio. Splitting callers this way keeps a chatty consumer from crowding out a careful one, and makes the per-caller budget reviewable in one file. Add your own; these two are examples.
